title: Rescue Me from Evil Men
superscription: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of David.

verses.text: Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men. Protect me from men of violence,
who devise evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long.
They sharpen their tongues like snakes; the venom of vipers is on their lips. Selah
Guard me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked. Keep me safe from men of violence who scheme to make me stumble.
The proud hide a snare for me; the cords of their net are spread along the path, and lures are set out for me. Selah
I say to the LORD, "You are my God." Hear, O LORD, my cry for help.
O GOD the Lord, the strength of my salvation, You shield my head in the day of battle.
Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked; do not promote their evil plans, lest they be exalted. Selah
May the heads of those who surround me be covered in the trouble their lips have caused.
May burning coals fall on them; may they be thrown into the fire, into the miry pits, never to rise again.
May no slanderer be established in the land; may calamity hunt down the man of violence.
I know that the LORD upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy.
Surely the righteous will praise Your name; the upright will dwell in Your presence.

context.author: The title names David. Psalms 138-145 are the last group of David’s psalms in the book.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men. Protect me from men of violence, who devise evil in their hearts and stir up war all day long” (vv.1-2). “They sharpen their tongues like snakes; the venom of vipers is on their lips” (v.3). They set traps: “The proud hide a snare for me” (v.5). David holds on: “I say to the LORD, ‘You are my God.’” and “You shield my head in the day of battle” (vv.6-7). He asks God to turn their schemes back on them (vv.8-11), and ends in confidence: “I know that the LORD upholds justice for the poor and defends the cause of the needy. Surely the righteous will praise Your name” (vv.12-13).
context.custom: Hunters set nets and snares along paths (v.5), the same images used for slander and traps in court. A helmet shielded the head in battle (v.7), the most vulnerable part of a soldier.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 141: May my prayer be set before You like incense.
context.timelineBible: Paul quotes v.3 in his description of human sin: “The venom of vipers is on their lips” (Romans 3:13). James warns that the tongue is “full of deadly poison” (James 3:8). Paul calls salvation a helmet (Ephesians 6:17).

gospelParallels.note: The venom of vipers is on their lips.

otBackground.note: Death and life in the tongue.

overview.summary: David asks God to rescue him from violent men with snake-like tongues and hidden traps, trusting the LORD who shields him in battle and upholds justice for the poor.
overview.settingLine: Snares on the path, a shield over the head.

archaeology.t: Assyrian reliefs show soldiers with pointed bronze helmets.
Bronze serpents and cobra amulets from Canaan and Egypt.

overview.discussion: David says, “You are my God” (v.6) when surrounded by traps. What do I need to say to God about the snares I face?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
